issues.legal_issue: Property given to a Hindu woman in lieu of maintenance under a post-Act compromise becomes her absolute property when she is placed in possession, despite restrictions in the compromise.
material_facts: A compromise made after the Hindu Succession Act came into force gave the woman land in lieu of maintenance and placed her in possession.
The compromise restricted her ability to sell or mortgage the land and described her interest as limited.
She remained in possession and enjoyment of the land and later sold part of it.
The plaintiffs sought possession on the basis that the woman had only a limited interest in the land.
issues.conclusion: The land became the woman's absolute property when she was placed in possession, notwithstanding the restrictions in the compromise; the appeal was allowed and the suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, read with its Explanation, property possessed by a female Hindu includes property acquired in lieu of maintenance and is held by her as full owner. Section 14(2) is confined to property acquired for the first time as a grant without a pre-existing right where the grant's terms prescribe a restricted estate; it does not apply to property acquired in lieu of a pre-existing right to maintenance. Under Section 14(1), a post-Act grant in lieu of maintenance becomes absolute when the woman is placed in possession despite restrictive terms. The Court applied V. Tulasamma v. V. Sesha Reddi, reiterated in later decisions, and referred to Jagannathan Pillai v. Kunjithapadam Pillai and Mangat Mal v. Punni Devi; it distinguished Gumpha v. Jaibai, which concerned property given under a will.

predicates.civil_appeal_challenging_limited_estate: A civil appeal challenges a decision treating property held by a woman as only a limited estate.
predicates.hindu_woman_received_property_for_mainte: A Hindu woman received the property in lieu of a right to maintenance.
predicates.woman_was_placed_in_possession: The woman was placed in possession of the property.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal challenges a limited-estate ruling and a Hindu woman received property in lieu of maintenance and was placed in possession, the rule treats her as its absolute owner.
